description: Caesium is a soft, silvery-golden alkali metal with symbol Cs and atomic number 55. It has a melting point of 28.5°C, making it one of only five elemental metals that are liquid at or near room temperature. It is the least electronegative stable element and has the largest atomic radius of all elements whose radii have been measured or calculated.
uses: Caesium is widely used in highly accurate atomic clocks and has been used to define the basic unit of time, the second, since 1967. Since the 1990s, the largest application has been as caesium formate for drilling fluids, with additional uses in electricity production, electronics, and chemistry. The radioactive isotope caesium-137 is used in medical applications, industrial gauges, and hydrology.
characteristics: Caesium is pyrophoric and reacts with water explosively even at temperatures as low as −116°C. It is highly ductile and the softest of all solid elements at room temperature with a Mohs hardness of 0.2. Its golden colour results from the decreasing frequency of light required to excite electrons, and it has a low boiling point of 641°C, the lowest of all stable metals other than mercury.
